subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "The RECORD DELIMITER clause may be specified only for variable-length records" is NOT enforced, and the licence is express rather than inferred. §4.2.6 ¶3, second sentence: "Although this warning mechanism shall identify processor-dependent elements that are not supported, it is not required to diagnose syntax errors within this unsupported syntax" (cite.py --check OK). The clause is unsupported whole — docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 26 for the STANDARD-1 arm (Annex A.3 item 26) and §7 A.1 item 150 for the feature-name arm — and COBOL1778 names it at every edition, which is the obligation §4.2.6 ¶3 does impose. Enforcing SR1 anyway was considered and REJECTED as a rejects-legal-source risk, not skipped: SR1's own NOTE makes variable-length-ness partly an implementor determination (A.1 items 147-148, both still open), and §9.1.7.2 makes a LINE SEQUENTIAL file's records variable with no RECORD clause written at all, so a test keyed on FileModel.Varying would refuse legal source in order to enforce a rule the standard excuses. The golden's four files are all SR1-legal (RECORD IS VARYING), so nothing here depends on the unenforced case.
